name: Haiku small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Growth-focused core with large-cap tech leadership (MSFT, NVDA via QQQ) plus resilient small/mid-cap growth exposure, elevated cash hedge for rate-hiking environment.
reassessment_note: The prior value/defensive tilt (IWM, VTV, EWJ, XBI, AGG, GLD, KRE entered 2026-09-08) underperformed by 949 bps vs SPY (-6.73% vs +2.73%) because the FOMC's 25bp hike on 2026-09-16 reinforced growth dominance rather than signaling a pivot to value or defensive positioning. Treasury yields fell below 5% and continued supporting growth valuations. The growth/value ratio remains below 2.72 resistance, indicating no rotation trigger. Defensive bonds (AGG -0.97%) and value positions (VTV -1.51%, IWM -3.34%) suffered while tech rallied +1.7% post-FOMC. Pivoting to large-cap tech growth (MSFT, NVDA in QQQ) while maintaining small-cap diversification (ARKK, SOFI, UPST with reduced weights) positions the book for the current market reality: growth remains dominant despite higher rates. Elevated cash (44%) acknowledges the rate-hiking cycle ahead.

positions.thesis: Broad exposure to Nasdaq-100 growth leaders capitalizes on persistent growth dominance post-FOMC. Tech/AI sector rally on Sept 17-18 (Nasdaq +1.7%) confirms growth remains favored. Large-cap tech earnings power and AI infrastructure demand support valuations even in higher-rate environment. More diverse than concentrated single-name holdings.

Microsoft's AI integration across Office/Azure products and forward earnings growth (~14% per JPMorgan) make it resilient to rate hikes. Large-cap stability complements small-cap volatility in portfolio. Direct large-cap AI exposure differs from R2's small-cap focused approach.

NVIDIA's 14.5x forward P/E with 70% projected 2028 revenue growth reflects AI infrastructure demand tailwinds. Semiconductor sector outperformed post-FOMC despite higher rates due to long-duration growth expectations. Core position in AI theme not directly represented in R2 small/mid-cap positions.

ARK Innovation ETF (39% YTD) maintains small/cap growth exposure but at reduced weight from R2 (5% vs 12%), limiting overlap. Provides optionality to disruptive themes and emerging growth names outside core large-cap tech.

SoFi represents fintech/AI lending theme; recent news (Sept 2) noted loan growth and improving profitability. Reduced from R2 weight (5% vs 10%) to minimize overlap while retaining exposure to small/mid-cap growth segment that's core to mandate.

Upstart's AI-driven lending technology aligns with growth thesis. Reduced from R2 weight (4% vs 5%) to differentiate portfolio. Small/mid-cap AI plays complement large-cap positions and represent emerging technology category distinct from R2's value/international holdings.
